text:
oliver_h: Pinging support — customer reported CI failure fetching our v2 tag. Error: `go: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk@v2.0.1: malformed module path or not found`

emily_w: Can you paste their go.mod + the replace they used?

oliver_h: Repro steps from customer (short):
1) checkout their repo
2) set GOPROXY (default) on CI
3) go build -> fails

Their go.mod:
```
module github.com/acme/inc-app

require (
	github.com/redwood-inference/sdk v2.0.1
)

replace github.com/redwood-inference/sdk => ../local/sdk
```

They said local dev works but CI (GHA runners) fails.

jgonzalez: That looks like a classic v2 module path mismatch. If your module has major v2, the module path inside `sdk` must be `github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/v2`. If tag is v2.0.1 but go.mod lacks `/v2`, proxies and the go tool can behave oddly, especially when `replace` is involved.

oliver_h: I inspected the tagged repo for v2.0.1 — the `go.mod` in the tag has `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk` (no `/v2`). So the tag doesn't match module path.

emily_w: Confirmed. That's why GOPROXY can't reconcile the module root and the v2 tag; local builds can succeed with `replace` pointing to a local dir, but CI using GOPROXY fetches the tag and errors.

ryan_p: Short-term workarounds for the customer:
- Update their replace to point to the v2 module path if their local copy has `/v2` in go.mod: `replace github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/v2 => ../local/sdk`
- Or remove `replace` and vendor the dependency for CI.

jgonzalez: Long-term we should: 1) cut a new v2.x release where `sdk/go.mod` module path ends with `/v2`, 2) add a CI guard in our release pipeline that validates module path vs tag major, 3) communicate to customers in the release notes.

deploy-bot: Checked release artifacts for `sdk v2.0.1` — go.mod module line: `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk` — anomaly flagged. Created internal issue RN-358.

support-bot: Created support ticket SR-9123 and assigned to eng-module-team. Priority P2.

emily_w: Options to fix the tagged release: 
- Do NOT force-push to fix tags (breaking history). Preferred: publish a new `v2.0.2` release with correct `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/v2` and document the migration.
- If absolutely necessary, we could create a compat pseudo-module, but that will be confusing.

oliver_h: I'll reply to the customer with the workaround and ETA for an official release: include sample `replace` snippet and note to remove replace in CI. Sample: 
```
// in customer's go.mod
replace github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/v2 => ../local/sdk
```

oliver_h: Reply sent. CC @jgonzalez for follow-up on the release pipeline checks.

ryan_p: I'll file an internal task to add a release-time check: if tag major != module path major then fail the release and require manual override.

jgonzalez: Thanks all — logging notes in the release postmortem and update the support ticket with planned v2.0.2. :thumbsup:
